claims: Comcast has agreed to a $117.5 million class-action settlement.
The cyberattack exposed the personal data of approximately 30 million Xfinity customers.
Individuals eligible for the settlement are those notified by Xfinity that their personal information was compromised in the October 2023 breach.
Eligible customers can receive up to $10,000 in reimbursement for documented out-of-pocket losses.
Eligible customers can receive up to $150 for lost time ($30 per hour for up to 5 hours).
Eligible customers can receive a $50 flat cash payment if they did not experience direct out-of-pocket losses.
Eligible customers can receive three years of free identity defense and restoration services.
Claims must be submitted by August 14, 2026.
A final approval hearing is scheduled for July 7, 2026.
Customers who do not submit a claim or opt out remain part of the class.
Such customers will not receive a cash payment.
Such customers may still enroll in the free identity protection services.
The lawsuit alleges Comcast failed to secure customer data.
Comcast has denied the allegation that it failed to secure customer data.
